thread:
lia: quick thread — customer asks + roadmap tradeoff. Acme is pushing for a 99.9% P95 < 300ms for text-gen on our hosted API for seq len ~2048. they want SLA language. need decision for launch criteria and fallback behavior.

sam: do we have any benchmark numbers for seq=2048 on current model/infra?
matt: rough numbers: p95 is ~220ms on GPU pool when batch size = 4 and cache hit > 60%. p99 jumps to ~900ms with KV churn.
rachel: Acme explicitly said if p99 > 500ms they'll consider a dedicated contract. their main ask is consistent tail latency — not absolute p50.
lia: thanks — key questions: 1) what graceful-degrade options are realistic for hosted without dedicated capacity; 2) what acceptance criteria do we commit to in the PRD for GA; 3) rollback/apply policy for bad regressions?
sam: graceful degrade ideas: - dynamic batching thresholds per model variant - fallback to smaller model (quantized) for paths that exceed tail threshold - background async prefill (prefetch KV) for long conversations
matt: add: route long sequences to a "slow-path" queue with higher CPU/GPU resources but lower concurrency; set a soft limit and return 202 + progress for extremely long sync requests.
rachel: any user experience concerns? Acme wants transparent behavior: they prefer a clear header/response indicating fallback used and expected latency.
lia: proposed PRD acceptance criteria (draft): - GA SLA: p95 < 300ms for seq<=1024, p95 < 500ms for seq<=2048 on hosted with noted workload profile - For requests that hit fallback: response includes header `X-Redwood-Fallback: <reason>` and a 5xx-free rate of 99.5% - Rollout: 10% canary -> 50% -> 100% with auto-rollback if p95 increases by >15% or error-rate increases >0.5%
sam: technical questions on rollout: how do we measure the baseline for % increases? need clear calc: baseline rolling 1h median p95 per route. also need a way to label requests that were served by fallback to exclude them from baseline.
matt: suggested rollout config snippet: ```yaml
canary: 0.1
metrics:
  - name: p95
    window: 1h
    trigger_increase_pct: 15
  - name: error_rate
    window: 1h
    trigger_increase_abs: 0.5
exclude_labels: [fallback=true]
```
lia: perfect — add that to the RFC. edge cases: - KV cache cold starts on model switch - bursts from many small requests causing convoying - customer pinned to older model where fallback is incompatible
rachel: for Acme negotiation: offer a dedicated Dedicated trial: 30 days with SLA backstop while they assess. For hosted PRD, include known capacity caveats in the docs.
sam: implementation notes: we need an internal flag to annotate fallback type (model-fallback, batch-threshold, queue-slowpath). telemetry work required ASAP.
lia: acceptance checklist to land in the PRD section: - benchmarks for seq 512/1024/2048 documented with test harness + scripts - rollout config + abort conditions added to deploy playbook - response header spec and customer-facing docs - telemetry labels + dashboard for fallback types - SLO/SLA wording reviewed with legal
matt: :thumbsup: I'll stub the dashboard and add alerts.
rachel: I'll run the customer negotiation thread with Acme and propose the 30-day dedicated trial.
deploy-bot: deploy started: rollout canary 0.1 for `slo-degrade-proposal` feature-flag — expected complete: 10m — monitor p95 and error_rate. :rocket:
lia: thanks everyone — I'll create the RFC PR with the draft acceptance criteria above and tag you for review. :eyes:
